format: RGBA16Float (uint16 little-endian bit patterns), row-major, index = (px + py*face_size)*4 + channel
face_convention: matches THREE.CubeTexture images order; texel (px,py) -> u,v=((idx+0.5)/size)*2-1 in [-1,1]; row 0 = v=-1 (flipY=false, matches app/src/field/bakeCube.ts)

channels.R: signed elevation in metres, raw (no log encoding, no clamping of negatives -- seafloor depth is real content, not a defect)
channels.G: area-weighted fraction (0..1) of contributing ETOPO 60-arcsec source cells satisfying is_grounded(bed_elev, surface_elev) -- a real land-fraction mask, matching the app's existing landFraction semantics (continuous, clamp01-blended, not boolean). Registered pixel-for-pixel with R via the same box-average+bilinear machinery, so a given texel's R and G always come from the same source cells. NOT derived from R: bed elevation's sign alone misclassifies ice sheets sitting on below-sea-level bedrock (e.g. West Antarctica) as ocean -- see module docstring for the probe table that demonstrated this. is_grounded is an Archimedes flotation test (bed + (rho_ice/rho_water)*(surface-bed) > 0, rho_ice/rho_water=0.917) applied ALONE, with no extra surface_elev>=0 clause -- two earlier versions of this rule were each wrong in a different way and both shipped before this one: (1) a bare ice-thickness test (surface-bed>1.0) fired on any floating ice regardless of depth, misclassifying open ocean under floating sea ice as land (the Greenland/Baffin Bay hard-edged-rectangle bug); (2) replacing it with is_grounded but keeping a `surface_elev>=0 OR` clause still misclassified floating ICE SHELVES as land, because a floating shelf has positive freeboard by construction (~8% of its thickness pokes above the waterline) -- measured ~1,000,000 of 233,280,000 source cells (~0.43% of Earth, concentrated at 60-85S: Ross, Ronne-Filchner, Amery, Larsen C) wrongly land under (2) alone. is_grounded with no OR clause fixes both: for the ordinary no-ice case it reduces exactly to bed_elev>0, so dry land is unaffected. Do not add back either a thickness-only test or a surface>=0 clause. KNOWN LIMITATION (do not 'fix' by adjusting the rule): sub-texel endorheic below-datum basins (Death Valley -86 m, Turpan, the Dead Sea) read as water -- each is far smaller than a source cell at every tier shipped here (Death Valley ~15 km wide vs 9.77 km/texel), and rasterizing coastline vectors to fix it would add a geo-stack dependency this pipeline deliberately does not have.
channels.A: validity: always 1.0 -- ETOPO 2022 60" declares a -99999 nodata sentinel that is never actually present (see nodata_audit below, exhaustively verified over all 233,280,000 source pixels)

surface_source.note: used only to compute the G-channel land mask (compute_land_mask) -- not baked into any channel directly.

validation.note: a single signed volume-integral ratio is a weak check here (land and ocean volumes are within an order of magnitude of each other and partially cancel) -- abs/land/ocean ratios don't share that cancellation risk and should all be checked, not just the first one
